What NoCharge V2 stores in your browser

NoCharge V2 does not retain game scores. Its theme providers store interface preferences; the separate Storage Inspector lists only a narrow set of key names.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 27, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Check the current platform.

Use the public pages behind this explanation.

Open the ArcadeReview PrivacyKeyboard-only play notes

Bottom line: The current V2 source does not save game scores or completed-board history. It uses browser storage for theme preferences, not a score archive or account record.

Theme preference keys

The base theme provider reads and writes nocharge-theme with a value of system, light, or dark. The seasonal provider uses nocharge-seasonal-mode with auto or standard. Browser privacy settings can make local storage unavailable; the interface still has an in-memory preference for the current page.

The Storage Inspector has a different filter

The tool at Storage Inspector runs only after a button press. It enumerates key names beginning with nocharge:, excludes the exact nocharge:consent name, and never reads stored values or changes browser data. The two theme keys above use hyphens, not a colon, so this filter will not list them. An empty result is not a complete storage inventory.

This is a narrow description of current source behavior, not a replacement for the Privacy page.
